status: post-hoc mechanistic diagnostic motivated by the temporal-content interaction result
purpose: Quantify retention-matched output divergence caused by changing the retained evidence sequence arrangement while holding the temporal-coordinate assignment common.
data_source: Existing Replication A 3x3 matrices only; no new policy inference.

factorial_cells.Y_AA: row A evidence sequence with temporal-coordinate assignment A
factorial_cells.Y_AB: row A evidence sequence with temporal-coordinate assignment B
factorial_cells.Y_BA: row B evidence sequence with temporal-coordinate assignment A
factorial_cells.Y_BB: row B evidence sequence with temporal-coordinate assignment B

interpretation.sequence_to_native_ratio_near_one: sequence-arrangement divergence under common temporal coordinates has magnitude comparable to the native matched residual; this does not by itself establish that sequence arrangement explains the native residual because direction and interaction must also be considered.
interpretation.sequence_to_native_ratio_much_below_one: sequence-arrangement divergence under common temporal coordinates is smaller than the native matched residual; the remainder cannot be uniquely assigned to temporal coordinates because temporal-by-sequence interaction may contribute.
interpretation.negative_or_low_sequence_vector_cosine: the effect of sequence arrangement depends strongly on the temporal-coordinate context.
interpretation.positive_mean_sequence_projection: on average, the controlled sequence-arrangement contrasts point in the direction of the native matched residual.
interpretation.scope: initial inferred 16x8 action chunk only; no behavioral claim and no additive variance-share interpretation.

process_handling.role: P1/P2/P3 are technical nuisance repeats, not scientific N.
process_handling.procedure: Compute each nonlinear metric independently in P1, P2, and P3, then average the three scalar metric values for each episode x unordered condition pair.

analysis_boundary: This is the final retrospective mechanistic localization analysis before synthesis and selection of a prospective behavioral or held-out validation experiment.
